source.title: A human brain network specialized for abstract formal reasoning

confidence_rationale: Methodologically the strongest imaging work in this pull -- deep-data precision fMRI, 24 participants, 10 experiments, with a near-zero Dice overlap (0.02 whole-brain, 0.04 frontal) between the abstract-reasoning network and the Multiple Demand network. It is cited in ARC-113's own source material. But its mapping to ARC-113 is INDIRECT: it dissociates reasoning from OTHER cognitive systems rather than dissociating the stages WITHIN the rule pipeline, which is what ARC-113 asserts. The within-reasoning deduction/induction split in MD engagement is the part that bears on the claim directly, and it is a secondary finding. Preprint status also caps source quality.
failure_signatures: The abstract reasoning network responded robustly and SIMILARLY during both deductive and inductive reasoning, during matrix problems, and during multiplication and division -- so at network resolution this evidence is equally consistent with ONE general abstract-reasoning module, which is the collapsed reading ARC-113 denies.

The dissociation demonstrated is between reasoning and non-reasoning systems (language, MD, intuitive physics, social), not among stages of a rule pipeline; a study of this design could not detect stage collapse within the reasoning network even if it were total.
The authors note they sampled only neurologically healthy educated adults from an industrialized culture and question generalisation across populations and other reasoning types.

mapping.source_claim_statement: A network of frontal brain areas supporting abstract formal reasoning robustly dissociates from the domain-general Multiple Demand network as well as from the language, intuitive physical reasoning, and social reasoning networks; the network responds during both deductive and inductive reasoning, matrix problems, and arithmetic. The Multiple Demand network was engaged by inductive reasoning and matrix problems but not by deductive syllogisms.
mapping.ree_translation: Abstract reasoning is not absorbed into a general-purpose executive resource: it has its own substrate, distinct from working-memory/fluid-intelligence machinery and from language. For ARC-113 this is second-order support -- it establishes that the rule pipeline is a real functional object that does not collapse into domain-general control. The directly relevant detail is the asymmetry in MD engagement: inductive reasoning and matrix problems recruited MD while deductive syllogisms did not, which is a dissociation BETWEEN reasoning operations and therefore evidence that apprehension-type and derivation-type stages draw on different resources.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The strongest and most-replicated result here is orthogonal to ARC-113: it separates reasoning from language and MD, whereas ARC-113 asserts non-collapse among stages INSIDE reasoning. Read carelessly this entry would be over-counted as support. Precision fMRI resolves networks, not pipeline stages, so a single abstract-reasoning network responding to everything is exactly what a collapsed-stage architecture would also produce -- the evidence does not discriminate. Preprint, not yet peer reviewed.
mapping.source_context: 24 participants (mean age 26.4, 14 female), deep-data precision fMRI, 1-3 sessions of 2-3 hours each, 10 fMRI experiments; deductive syllogisms, inductive reasoning, matrix reasoning, arithmetic.

confidence_components.notes: High source quality (precision fMRI, large per-subject data, explicit network-overlap statistics) offset by the lowest mapping fidelity in this pull, since the headline dissociation is between systems rather than between pipeline stages. For an architectural claim mapping_fidelity dominates, hence the modest aggregate.
